newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo railway land sale may lift Japan land market.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo railway land sale may lift Japan land market.

text.p: Monday's auction of three tracts of land in central Tokyo once owned by the defunct Japanese National Railways could fetch up to 300 billion yen -- a sum which would boost sentiment in Japan's sluggish real estate market, analysts said.
Analysts said they expect the prime pieces of land located near Ginza, Tokyo's premier shopping area, to be priced at a total of between 200 billion yen and 300 billion yen.
A figure at the higher end of this range would indicate that Japan's land prices have bottomed out, they said.

The auction results for the some 53,000 square metres of idle land once used as the Shiodome freight station will be announced at 4.30 p.m. Tokyo time (0730 GMT). The land is being auctioned by the JNR Settlement Corp.

Two foreign consortiums are rumoured to be among those bidding for the land, and analysts said if one or both were successful in bidding it would show that foreigners believed that Japan's land prices were relatively attractive.
"This would be a boon to the market," said one analyst.
They also said the sale could help stocks in Japan's ailing bank sector.
Japanese banks' struggles with a mountain of bad loans, many of which were made to the real estate sector, could only benefit if signs of life emerged in the land market, they said.

"If the land sells for 300 billion yen that would indicate that the real estate market has bottomed out, and that would be good for stocks in the real estate, banking and securities sectors," said an analyst at a major brokerage.
Japan's land prices have been falling since the "bubble economy" of sky-high stock and land prices burst in the early 1990s.
